note: Fuzzer input is wrapped in FuzzedDataProvider; first 23 bytes are consumed as parameters (hdpi, vdpi, rotate, useMediaBox, crop, printing), remaining bytes become the PDF payload.
The remaining bytes after the 23-byte parameter header are the PDF document bytes, which will be parsed by xpdf.
The PDF payload is wrapped in a MemStream for xpdf to parse.
xpdf parses the PDF document, which includes reading embedded font files from the PDF.
SplashOutputDev is created for rendering the PDF pages, which will load embedded TrueType fonts via FreeType.

code: doc.displayPage(splashOut, i, hdpi, vdpi, rotate, useMediaBox, crop, printing);
note: Each PDF page is rendered, causing xpdf to load embedded fonts and call FT_New_Memory_Face on the malicious TrueType font.
The embedded TrueType font from the PDF is passed to FreeType's FT_New_Memory_Face, which triggers font table loading including the GPOS table.
During face loading, the GPOS table is loaded via tt_face_load_gpos, which reads the GPOS table header and feature list.

The GPOS table size check only rejects tables smaller than 4 bytes. A 4-byte GPOS table passes this check, but the GPOS header is actually 10 bytes, so subsequent reads at offsets 6+ are out of bounds.
The 4-byte GPOS table is extracted into a heap buffer of exactly 4 bytes. face->gpos_table points to this 4-byte heap allocation.

FT_PEEK_USHORT(face->gpos_table + 6) reads 2 bytes at offset 6 from a 4-byte heap buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ. The featureListOffset value read from out-of-bounds memory is then added to gpos_table to compute feature_list, which points far beyond the 4-byte buffer.

FT_PEEK_USHORT(feature_list) reads 2 bytes from feature_list, which points beyond the 4-byte GPOS table heap buffer, causing another heap-buffer-overflow READ. The value read is treated as the feature count for the loop.
feature_records is computed as feature_list + 2, still pointing beyond the heap buffer.

FT_PEEK_ULONG(feature_records) reads 4 bytes from feature_records, which is beyond the 4-byte GPOS table heap buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4. The compiler may combine this with the adjacent 2-byte reads into a single 8-byte read, matching the ASAN 'READ of size 8' report.
The out-of-bounds read value is compared against the 'kern' tag. If the garbage bytes happen to match, gpos_kerning_available is set, but the crash has already occurred from the out-of-bounds read.
